messages:
olivia: Kicked off an offline replay to test a combo: queue priors (age+kv), KV prefetch on hot keys, and a token-budget sweep (8/16/32). A/B against baseline (fifo, no-prefetch). replay-bot posted run IDs and artifact links.

rajeev: Nice. Can you paste the replay config and which trace set you used? Want to verify we didn't mix session-level traces.

marta: Using trace set: prod-sampled-2026-02 (30k sessions, mix of short chat + long completion). Config attached below.
```
# replay config
queue_policy: priority_age
queue_priors:
  - name: kv_hot
    weight: 1.5
  - name: short_seq
    weight: 1.2
token_budget_targets: [8, 16, 32]
kv_prefetch: enabled
kv_prefetch_window: 64
kernel_selection_hint: auto
metrics: [p50_latency, p95_latency, tokens_per_gpu, kv_hit_rate]
```

olivia: replay-bot -> run 1765007890-01 (baseline), 1765007890-02 (priors+prefetch, tb=16). Artifacts: s3://rwd-replays/1765007890/* . infra-bot also printed simulator config and seed.

eva: Quick sanity check: prefetch_window=64 corresponds to prefetching up to 64 recent tokens for active sessions? That can increase memory pressure on some kernels.

marta: Right — we limited prefetch to sessions with kv_hit_rate > 0.2 in the trace to avoid cold start bloat. Also added a soft cap so aggregate KV prefetch tokens per-GPU won't exceed 1M.

tom: Any changes in kernel selection logs? We expect more packed kernels (batch-level) when short_seq prior gets weight.

olivia: Good catch. From the replay logs: kernel_selector moved from custom_f32 -> packed_int8 for ~42% of tokens in the priors run. For the tb=8 sweep, packed_int8 usage jumped to 55% but p95 latency degraded for long tails.

rajeev: Can you paste the perf summary? Even a small table helps.

marta: Summary (A = baseline fifo, B = priors+prefetch tb=16):
- p50: A=28ms, B=24ms (-14%)
- p95: A=190ms, B=167ms (-12%)
- tokens_per_gpu: A=1.00 (norm), B=1.05 (+5%)
- kv_hit_rate: A=0.18, B=0.29 (+11ppt)
- kernel_mix: A={custom_f32:68%, packed_int8:22%, xformers:10%}, B={custom_f32:50%, packed_int8:42%, xformers:8%}

eva: Wow kv_hit moved up a lot. That explains token efficiency. But p95 improvement is less than p50, suggests tail-sensitive interactions (maybe queue head-of-line blocking).

olivia: We saw head-of-line cases when a long completion stayed at head but short high-priority requests queued. The queue_prior implementation uses age+weight but we didn't implement starvation damping. Adding a starvation counter reduced p95 regressions.

rajeev: Did you simulate starvation damping? What was the policy?

marta: Implemented damping: each request gains a damping_score after X seconds in queue; effective_priority = base_priority * (1 + min(damping_score, 0.5)). X=0.5s in the replay. Results: p95 for B improved from 167ms -> 153ms.

tom: Any changes to kernel selection after damping?

olivia: Packed_int8 share dropped slightly to 38% after damping, but overall GPU utilization remained similar. Token efficiency still +4% vs baseline.

replay-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://rwd-replays/1765007890/artefact-manifest.json ; summary -> gist: https://gist.redwood/1765007890/replay-summary (internal).

marta: One weird regression: for tb=8 (aggressive small budgets) some sessions triggered fallback kernels (xformers) more often due to quantization quality checks failing at longer contexts, which increased latency for those sessions. TL;DR: tb=8 helps p50 but harms a subset of long-context requests.

olivia: Action items proposal:
- Keep priors+prefetch with damping as default in staging.
- Run an additional sweep around token_budget 12 and 20 (narrowing).
- Add a kernel-quality postcheck in the replay harness to flag cases where quantized kernels increase decode time or degrade outputs.
- Create alert to catch head-of-line > 2s in live queues.

rajeev: +1. Also capture per-model sequence-length distribution to auto-tune token_budget target per-model. Could avoid tb=8 harming long-contexts.

eva: I'll take the kernel-quality postcheck. Will add a small eval that runs golden prompts through both kernels and compares logits drift + walltime.

tom: I'll add the per-model seq-length hist export to the replay manifest and hook it into Optimize.

olivia: Great. I'll open PRs for the damping change and the narrow sweep. Posting links once ready. :thumbsup: :bar_chart:
